features: Leaning facet sketch on the top
field_notes: Field-sampled: the surface itself carries no undercut at this parting.

30.2% of the surface carries less than 3.0 deg of draft or stands parallel to the pull (6.9% marginal, 23.3% vertical). It releases, but it drags on the sand and will want a longer rap. Raise the crown or square the sides to steepen it.
Extrude "Bright-cut facet" (#8) is drilled at the bench: drill mark on the parting line at 90°; the hole's centre is 0.5 mm toward the low edge (a dot there leaned to -38° over 0.31 mm²).
Mirror "Mirror the facet" (#9) is drilled at the bench: drill mark on the parting line at 90°; the hole's centre is 0.5 mm toward the high edge (a dot there leaned to -38° over 0.31 mm²).
Judged with the ring as built: 1 CAD part (1 joined, 0 cut) at the parting plane z = +0.00 mm — 57.5 mm² of part surface, 0.0 mm² of it undercut.

Press-pull "Chamfer the rim" (#6): 0.0 mm² of undercut leaning to -1° on flanks facing back across the parting plane, 72–108°, 1.4 mm toward the low edge to 1.4 mm toward the high edge — stage it Bench to solder it on after the pour (the pattern keeps a locating mark), or move it onto the parting line.

verdict_cause.lesson: The verdict is the lesson, and it has two sources. Pulled along the finger in two-part Delft sand, a flat band's broad crest stands square to the pull: the bare Flat 6.0 x 2.0 already reads 'Castable with care' at 30.2% drag, past the 12% the verdict allows. The cartouche adds its own zero-draft faces: its flat top and its two end walls face round the ring, square to the pull like a signet's table, and its 12 deg draft helps only the two long walls that face across the finger. That is 24.5 of its 57.5 mm2 standing vertical, taking the ring to 30.9% drag and 'Castable with care', with 0 obstructions and 0 unresolved rays at 0.100 and 0.075 mm: it releases, but drags and wants a longer rap. Its 0.029 mm2 judged undercut (worst -1.0 deg) is tessellation on the faceted chamfer corners, below the 0.075 mm ray grid. The cartouche alone carries the verdict on a domed band: the same history on Rivet's LowDome 6.0 x 2.1 turns a 'Castable' band (4.4% drag) into 'Castable with care' (6.7%). No draft angle on the boss can make it Castable; only a draft on the top and the end walls, or another pull, would.
